result.title: Heading Hierarchy Reconstruction for Complex and Long Documents with Level-Wise Multimodal Memory
result.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) have been widely adopted for document parsing and optical character recognition (OCR), as they can accurately extract page-level elements. However, downstream applications such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) also require coherent document-level structure. Although these models indicate heading levels using different numbers of preceding ``\#'' symbols, page-by-page prediction often lacks document-level consistency. In practice, input-resolution and context-length constraints make it infeasible for a VLM to jointly process all page images in documents containing tens or hundreds of pages. To address this limitation, we propose a VLM-based framework that incrementally reconstructs heading hierarchies with a \emph{level-wise multimodal memory}. The memory retains a compact subset of all previously processed pages, selected by anchors. Our framework supports flexible anchor selection, and in this work we select the most recent node at each level, allowing the VLM to observe the visual, textual, and layout patterns of headings at every level. For comprehensive evaluation, we also introduce the Complex and Long Document Heading Hierarchy Reconstruction Benchmark (CLDoc-HHRBench), comprising 250 documents and 11,212 pages with expert-verified annotations. Experiments on CLDoc-HHRBench and three existing benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出基于 VLM 的框架，用「层级多模态记忆」按页增量重建长文档的标题层级，并构建了 CLDoc-HHRBench 基准（250 篇文档、11212 页）进行评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以锚点选取各级最近节点、用紧凑记忆维持跨页一致性的做法，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与缓存/状态压缩提供可核查的方法线索，但论文本身不涉及 latent 推理。
